reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 3 of 3). The plan is careful and its seams exist. land_or_block adds the Score at close (close.rs ~220-227). The gate rechecks each Score against expected_score (jobs.rs ~290-317). Rule::AppendOnly exists. RealSteps.lander, RecordingLander and real_steps_with exist, and the lander double gets an &Athena, so it can check records at head when called. land_pr does read verification and candidate at head (landing.rs 708-718). Athena's two out-of-deliverable file findings are weighed; the plan's reasons for run/mod.rs and main.rs are sound. Two major problems remain. First, dating the queue Score at close time loses any intervention made between close and landing: intervene writes no re-score when no Score exists (manage.rs 368-375), and the gate allows a re-score only in the commit that adds its intervention, so the plan's 'left for a re-score' premise is false. Dating the Score at landing time fixes it. Second, moving only the Score does not meet section 8 ('records order equals landing order, never refers to an unlanded job') or the reading's 'each landed job's records', yet criterion 6 would call job 8 built. The plan raises this as a BLOCKER question for the user; it must be answered and the criteria adjusted before production. Minor: publication on a squash-merge host is understated, and the descendant check in criterion 1 is weak. Findings: minor: crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs is not among the reading's deliverables (files, crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs); minor: crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs is not among the reading's deliverables (files, crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs); major: With the Score deferred, an intervention made between close and landing is never scored: intervene writes no re-score, and the queue Score dated at close time leaves it out. (Decision 4 (`at` = close time) and the Risks entry on `athena intervene --job`; crates/athena-core/src/manage.rs 366-375; crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs 271-285); major: Moving only the Score does not meet section 8 or the reading. Every other closing record still commits at close, before the host landing, in the order jobs finish, yet criterion 6 would call build job 8 'built'. (Approach, Decision 1 and open question 1; criterion 6 demonstration; docs/design/async-drain.md lines 214-216); minor: The publication limit is understated. On a squash-merge host, a job's queue Score appears inside the next job's squash commit, not after its own landing, and the last Score of a drain is never published. (Decision 3 and open question 3 (publication)); minor: The descendant check holds almost by construction, because the local landing commit is the close commit, which always comes before the lander call. It adds little evidence. (Criterion 1 demonstration: 'each Score commit is a descendant of its own landing commit on the first-parent chain')
